title: Provide Documentation on Setup with Google App Engine

comments.body: @tolot27, I'm not sure how to label this.

We will be adding documentation.
There are many subjects that need documentation.

@techbelle What should be setup on Google App Engine? xDrip is an Android application which gets build with Gradle. If you don't want to create an environment by yourself, you can try the Makefile provided in #903 or look at [.travis.yaml](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/blob/master/.travis.yml).

I don't have a question about how to set it up. This is a suggestion of, _there should be documentation on how to set this up_, in case users don't want to use Heroku. I set up Nightscout on Google App Engine a couple of years ago, there were many other users asking then how to do it.

But you cannot run xDrip at Google App Engine. Hence, there cannot be a documentation about it. Or I do not understand your question. Setting up [Nightscout CGM Monitor](https://github.com/nightscout/cgm-remote-monitor) at your own server, Heroku or somewhere else is a totally different topic. In that case you have to ask the Nightscout community for support.
ahh I see what you are saying. It did take quite a bit of effort to set up both (xDrip and Nightscout) end to end, but it's fine to keep this closed.
